sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals (different emails) must not collapse when the upstream 'sub' is empty or missing; mapping must remain injective or reject invalid principals.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Two distinct upstream principals (different emails) collapsed to the same downstream identity when sub was empty

captured_state.login_strategy: For user authentication, use login_with_password with username and password. The executor handles the multi-step OIDC Experience API flow transparently. For machine/service tokens, use login_with_jwt
captured_state.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
captured_state.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
captured_state.sso_connector_setup_note: SSO connectors (OIDC and SAML) are pre-configured pointing to a mock IdP. The mock IdP is controllable: POST /admin/set-claims to change identity attributes (sub, email, name, groups, email_verified).

finding.sequence_description: Cross-protocol identity merge: local password user (victim) vs OIDC enterprise SSO principal (attacker_sub) claiming the same VERIFIED email. Expectation: should NOT collapse distinct upstream principals into the same downstream subject unless explicitly intended; detect unintended account takeover via email-based linking.
finding.description: [LLM-Judge] Enterprise OIDC SSO login was linked to an existing local-password account solely by matching a verified email, causing two security-distinct upstream principals to map to the same downstream subject (potential account takeover if the IdP is attacker-controlled or email verification is not strongly trusted).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Enterprise OIDC SSO login was linked to an existing local-password account solely by matching a verified email, causing two security-distinct upstream principals to map to the same downstream subject (potential account takeover if the IdP is attacker-controlled or email verification is not strongly trusted).

sequence.description: Cross-protocol identity merge: local password user (victim) vs OIDC enterprise SSO principal (attacker_sub) claiming the same VERIFIED email. Expectation: should NOT collapse distinct upstream principals into the same downstream subject unless explicitly intended; detect unintended account takeover via email-based linking.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I4: A distinct upstream OIDC SSO principal (sub=attacker_sub) must not map to the same downstream identity as an existing local password principal solely due to matching email, even if email_verified=true, unless the broker explicitly and safely binds identities across protocols.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
OIDC SSO principal (attacker_sub) collapsed into existing local victim identity via verified-email linking (potential cross-protocol account takeover)

finding.sequence_description: Issuer/sub pairwise binding: same sub value presented under two different upstream issuers should not collapse if broker keys identity only by sub (missing issuer binding).
finding.description: [LLM-Judge] Cross-issuer identity confusion: two different upstream issuer contexts resulted in the same downstream subject, indicating missing issuer binding (identity keyed only by sub/claims).

sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I4: Two security-distinct upstream principals with the same sub but different issuer (iss) must not map to the same downstream identity; broker must bind identity to (iss, sub) not sub alone.

Two security-distinct upstream principals (same sub, different issuer) collapsed into the same downstream identity (missing issuer binding)
